entry.title: Caves of Qud: Diaspora to Launch as Steam's First Early Access DLC
entry.content:
Game Developer News | gamedeveloper.com | source

Freehold Games' expansion for Caves of Qud, titled Diaspora, will be released in Early Access on Steam. This is the first instance of a downloadable content (DLC) expansion launching via Steam's Early Access program rather than as a completed 1.0 release.

The developers intend to use the model to facilitate community stress-testing of the expansion's complex systems and to maintain a flexible development schedule. This strategy allows for incremental funding and iterative development based on player feedback.

entry.title: decomp.dev Disables Main Index and New Project Tracking
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | decomp.dev | discussion | hacker news

decomp.dev, a platform launched in 2024 to track matching decompilation progress, is disabling its main index and the ability to add new projects. While the site will continue to host historical data and individual project pages, it will no longer serve as a centralized aggregator or public leaderboard for active efforts.

The decision stems from the impact of advanced AI models on the decompilation community. The site's creator, @encounter, cites the rise of low-effort, hostile forks of existing projects and the "racing" of unrefined ports by actors utilizing AI as primary drivers. These trends have reportedly led to a conflation of research-focused decompilation with superficial game porting, which the developer argues undermines the community's focus on understanding original source code.

entry.title: Mythfall Implements Procedural Mumble Speech for NPCs
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | youtube.com | discussion

The developer of Mythfall, a browser-based bullet hell MMO, has implemented a procedural "mumble speech" system for non-player characters. Instead of using recorded audio files, the system generates real-time vocalizations based on text input by mathematically modeling vocal folds, mouth resonance, and airflow. This creates human-like, non-verbal speech that adjusts dynamically to the text being displayed.

This approach reduces download sizes and allows for seamless dialogue updates during development. The system utilizes existing text punctuation to dictate speech rhythm and intonation, using question marks for rising pitch and commas for pauses. By adjusting pitch and resonance parameters, the developer can create distinct character identities, such as children or elderly NPCs, within a minimal memory footprint.

entry.title: Epic Games Rebuilds Easy Anti-Cheat for Linux
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | onlineservices.epicgames.com | discussion | hacker news

The new "EAC Linux v2" implementation seeks to provide a level of anti-cheat protection on Linux comparable to the Windows version. This overhaul aims to enable multiplayer games like Fortnite to run on Linux by leveraging existing system security features—including TPM 2.0, Secure Boot, and eBPF—rather than relying on a dedicated kernel module.

A pilot program in Fortnite will precede the release of the technology to other game developers. To facilitate this, Epic Games is working with Linux distribution maintainers to integrate well-known signing keys into the secure boot process and is requiring specific hardware configurations such as IOMMU and Kernel Lockdown Integrity Mode.

entry.title: Shield Battery Implements Rollback Netcode for StarCraft: Brood War
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | youtube.com | discussion

Shield Battery has implemented rollback netcode for StarCraft: Brood War, replacing the traditional lockstep networking model. This system allows player commands to execute on the very next frame, significantly reducing the input latency experienced during online matches.

The netcode predicts player actions and only corrects the game state when unexpected commands arrive, transforming lag spikes into minor visual "hops" rather than total freezes. Additionally, latency adjustments are applied to each player's connection individually, ensuring that a single player's poor connection does not delay the entire match.

entry.title: Replacing SHA1 with xxHash Speeds Up Unreal Engine Editor Startup
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | larstofus.com | source | discussion

Replacing the SHA1 hashing algorithm with xxHash for shader source code reduces Unreal Engine editor startup times. Because shader source code is non-sensitive data, the cryptographically secure but computationally expensive SHA1 was deemed unnecessary for this specific task.

In performance testing on the "Electric Dreams" sample project, CPU time for the hashing process dropped from 12.90 seconds to 1.59 seconds, representing an eightfold speedup for that operation. Epic Games developers have reviewed and accepted the optimization as a pull request to the Unreal Engine codebase.

entry.title: Way of Rhea Developer Discusses Six-Year Development in Rust
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | gamesbymason.com | discussion

The creator of the puzzle game discusses the six-year process of building the project using the Rust programming language. The text covers the transition from C++, the creation of a custom engine featuring a built-in scripting language for hot swapping, and the selection of various crates to handle tasks like windowing and crash reporting.

Technical hurdles such as extended compile times and the limitations of the Steam Input API are examined alongside the decision to build a custom engine rather than using existing tools. The developer estimates that engine development required 20% to 30% of the total production time and argues that shipping a completed game is the ultimate way to test the efficacy of technical architectural choices.

entry.title: Nanolathe Open-Source Engine Rebuilds Total Annihilation for Modern Computers
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | nanolathe.gg | hacker news

Nanolathe is an open-source, MIT-licensed 2.5D RTS engine that reimplements Total Annihilation through clean-room research for modern hardware. It features a modern GPU renderer with enhanced lighting and detail, alongside a classic CPU renderer that replicates the original aesthetic.

The project is in public beta and offers a browser-based demo featuring three original missions. To access the full campaign, skirmish modes, or online multiplayer, users must install the native client on Windows, Mac, or Linux and provide their own game files from platforms like Steam or GOG.

entry.title: Pat Kerr Recreates 1996 Grand Theft Auto Vehicle Physics Prototype
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | patkerr.co.uk | discussion | hacker news

Programmer Pat Kerr has released a JavaScript recreation of the 2D physics simulation developed in 1996 that served as the basis for the vehicle systems in the original Grand Theft Auto. Titled "Motion Lab," the interactive demo allows users to test different dynamics through three modes: a car, a spaceship, and a brick.

The simulation utilizes 2D rigid body dynamics, including torques, to handle rotation and momentum more coherently than the simple point-physics models common in mid-1990s game development. To mimic the specific handling of early GTA vehicles, the model employs an approximate tyre resistance system to simulate lateral and longitudinal friction.
